prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1136; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Driver 1 was traveling through the intersection in Pearland, Texas, when the vehicle turned left and was struck by Driver 2, who was proceeding straight. Driver 1 was operating the vehicle at the time of the collision and was the only occupant in the driver's seat, with a Passenger seated beside him. On arrival, officers found both vehicles at rest near the intersection, with visible front-end damage to Driver 2's vehicle and a corresponding impact to the driver's side of Driver 1's vehicle, consistent with the reported angle and direction of travel. Driver 1 reported neck pain and stiffness shortly after the impact, and the nature of the injury appeared consistent with the force of a collision of this kind. Officers reviewed scene photographs, which confirmed several of the reported details. No independent witnesses were identified at the scene. Officers found no indication that the vehicle had sustained prior damage in the affected areas. Driver 1 is reported to reside in the same household as the policyholder and is listed as a covered household member.
